history.content: logging this i guess. been clearing out my dads old garage these past few weeks. found a box of his tools. feels kind of nostalgic
That sounds quietly nostalgic — like the box of tools carried a lot of him with it. Does it feel more warm, or a little tender too?
warm i think. mostly nostalgic yeah. he passed two years ago. the garage was the last thing left to sort out
Warm, and nostalgic — with the garage being the last thing left, it sounds like this might be tied to a little ending too. Does it feel more like a soft missing, or more like a heavy goodbye?

thats the thing. i keep calling it nostalgic or sad but its not really. closing the garage door yesterday i just felt. settled. like it was finally ok. organized his wrenches by size the way he liked. dont know why that mattered but it did
Settled makes sense here — like putting his wrenches in order gave the whole thing a kind of rightness. Does it feel more like relief, or more like quiet care?
quiet care probably. both maybe. relief that its done but i wasnt rushing. took my time with it. theres no more loose ends now. everything has a place. me and him are square

That has a very finished, steady shape — quiet care with relief, and a sense that everything has its place now. We can leave it here if you want, or I can stay with that “square” feeling a little longer.
nah i think thats it. square is the right word for it. funny i came in thinking i was sad and its more like peace. anyway. gonna go make dinner. thanks for this
That feels nicely settled — square seems to hold it. Enjoy dinner.
